texts: In the wayside inn of the world, the unknowing guest swears the borrowed room is his own forever.

Give me a doha about people who treat the inn of this world as their permanent dwelling, not knowing they are guests for a night, because the darkness of not-knowing makes them take the borrowed for their own.
doha on how clueless ppl think the inn of life is theirs to keep
My uncle keeps decorating a rented inn room he will leave next week, and it reminds me how people mistake the passing for the lasting; doha?
inn, not knowing
My friend is certain his neighbour has all the answers and refuses to check anything himself; it's sad how he believes whatever sounds sure.
doha on how people believe false stuff just bc they dont know better
mistaking false for true
In the dim hours of not-knowing, the false wears the face of the true and the heart bows to it.
I'd like a doha about the darkness of not knowing that makes a person take the false for the true, so that he clings to illusions, argues for them, and never suspects he is wrong.
The fool carries the philosopher's stone in his pocket and weaves rags at the weaver's loom, not knowing what he holds.
Write a doha about a man who owns the philosopher's stone but sits at the weaver's loom all his life making coarse stuff, because his ignorance hides from him the priceless thing in his own hands.
My cousin has a rare skill that could change his life, like the philosopher's stone, but he wastes it at a weaver's loom for pennies, simply because no one ever told him his worth.
doha: ppl dont know they hold the philosopher's stone, sitting at a weaver's loom
philosopher's stone, weaver's loom
Craft a doha about a man who sits in a boat full of holes and keeps bailing but never looks beneath his feet, because not-knowing makes him take the false cause for the real.
boat, not knowing
Aboard the boat, the sleepless one points at the far shore and never sees the hole beneath his own feet.
doha about being on a boat but not knowing where ur headed lol
My dad refuses to read the instructions for anything, and last weekend he took the boat out confidently in completely the wrong direction; it reminded me how sure ignorance feels.
My little brother mistook a curved root by the river for a snake and ran off screaming, and it made me think about how not-knowing makes us fear what isn't there.
doha: ignorance makes u see a snake where its just a river bend
Please make a doha about how a person who does not know the real nature of things fears a harmless thing as a snake and drowns in the river of illusion, because he takes the false for the true.
The unknowing see a snake in the ripple of the river, and flees from a ripple, never knowing it is only water.
river, snake, not knowing
pls a doha abt the darkness of not knowing, how we think wrong things r right
Unlit by understanding, the mind mistakes the passing for the lasting, the hollow for the full.

Compose a doha for a friend who keeps defending a belief he has never questioned, telling him gently that ignorance makes one take the false for the true and that the first step is to say I do not know.
I spent years sure of something about my family that turned out to be completely wrong, and the embarrassment of how blind I was still stings.
taking false for true
crossroads, lost man
At the crossroads of the world the unknowing stand, taking each signpost for the way and no road for the end.
I need a doha about a man at a crossroads who cannot tell which way is real because he has never learned to tell the false from the true, so he follows every shouting voice and gets nowhere.
doha: ppl at a crossroads follow whatever voice is loudest, cuz they dont know
Standing at the crossroads of my career, I realized I had been following advice from people who knew no more than I did, mistaking confidence for knowing.

Please write a doha for my younger brother who believes every viral message he reads without checking anything, so that he sees how not-knowing makes a person take the false for the true again and again.
doha about being clueless and fooled by ppl
My aunt gave a huge sum to a stranger who promised miracles, completely sure he was genuine, and I keep thinking of how not-knowing blinds people.
darkness of not-knowing
Where no understanding dawns, the false gleams like the true and the heart is fooled by the glitter.
He smears ash on his limbs and bows to the temple wall, mistaking the husk of the rite for the grain of the real.
A man in our town covers himself in ash and visits the temple daily, certain he is holy, but he has never asked himself what any of it means.

Can you put together a doha about a person who rubs ash on his body and visits the temple faithfully, yet remains in the darkness of not-knowing, because he takes outward ritual for real understanding.
doha: ash n temple wont help if ur clueless inside
ash, temple, not knowing
Write a doha about a fool who tosses away a thread of real gold, mistaking it for common string, and then treasures a worthless glitter, since not-knowing makes him take the false for the true.
My landlady kept a thin gold chain tied with plain thread to her keys all her life, never knowing its worth, and swore it was nothing; I think of such blindness often.
Gold lay twined in a common thread, and the unknowing hand cast both aside to chase a glitter.
doha w gold n thread, mistaking real for fake
gold, thread, ignorance
The chakor stares at the washerman's bleached bundle all night, taking it for its beloved light, and dies unknowing of the difference.
doha: chakor bird mistakes the washerman's white laundry for what it longs for
Give me a doha about a chakor bird that gazes at the bright wash of a washerman all night thinking it its beloved, a picture of the person who takes the false for the true and pines for nothing.
chakor bird, washerman, mistaken
My roommate fell for someone who was only pretending, like a chakor bird gazing at a washerman's bright laundry, and he still doesn't see it; doha?
fire, scales, ignorance
My uncle lost everything weighing goods on rigged scales and never saw it; he blamed fire, fate, and everyone but himself.
doha: clueless ppl cant read the scales, fire everywhere but they dont see
Fire at the hem, and still the blind one reads his scales and swears all is fine.
I'd like a doha about a man who weighs everything on crooked scales while a fire spreads around him, yet insists all is balanced and safe because he takes the false for the true.
doha: clueless ppl are like a fly stuck in something sweet
The fly alights on sweetness and cannot rise, never knowing the sweetness was its undoing.
Write a doha about the fly that sits on sweet syrup and is trapped, a picture of the unknowing person who takes pleasure for happiness and cannot see that the false sweetness is what holds him down.
fly, ignorance
My friend can't stop chasing short-lived thrills, like a fly drawn to something sweet, and he doesn't realize it is what keeps him stuck.
My neighbour sold a family pearl for a few coins thinking it was a useless trinket, and cried when he learned its worth; doha on that blindness?
doha: clueless guy throws away a pearl thinking its junk
Craft a doha about a pearl lying in the dust while the unknowing pass by, mistaking it for worthless dirt and picking up a glass bauble instead, because not-knowing fools them.
The pearl lay in the dust and the unknowing passed by; they bowed to glass because they could not tell the shine.
pearl, not knowing
taking false for true
Please make a doha for those who quarrel over things they have never understood, saying that ignorance is a dark room where everyone argues loudly and no one can see the other or the real.
Dark is the mind that does not know it does not know; it takes its dream for the dawn.
doha on how not knowing makes us confident about wrong things
At the family dinner everyone argued loudly about something none of them had actually looked into, and I just sat there thinking how sure people sound when they know nothing.
doha about being fooled by false stuff cuz u just dont know any better
Please write a doha about a village that follows a fake healer because nobody there knows enough to doubt him, showing how not-knowing is a darkness in which the false looks true.
I believed a rumor about my coworker for months and treated her badly, and when I found out the facts I felt ashamed of how easily I was fooled.
unknowing, fooled
Without the dawn of understanding, a rumor is honored as fact and a lie is welcomed as a guest.
O mind sunk in not-knowing, you call the passing days eternal and the borrowed breath your own.
short doha on ignorance making ppl cling to illusions
My grandfather lived his life certain of a story about our family that was never real, and nobody had the heart to correct him.

Write a doha about how the darkness of not-knowing makes human beings take the temporary for the permanent, the false for the true, and suffering for pleasure, so that they never wake from their long mistake.
blind to reality
doha about a fool who tries to cross a bridge made of moonbeams, clueless lol
I need a doha about a man who sees moonbeams on the bridge and tries to walk across them, a picture of the unknowing who chase appearances and fall for what is not there.
bridge, moon, ignorance
A friend of mine kept waiting for the moon to fix his bad luck instead of repairing a broken bridge near his village, so sure of his belief; doha?
He stares at the moon and trusts a bridge of moonbeams to carry him; the dark of not-knowing walks him to the edge.
The beggar sits inside a gilded cage, begging for a gate he never tried; such is the one who does not know.
beggar, cage, ignorance
doha: a beggar sitting in an open cage, begging, not knowing he is free
Can you put together a doha about a beggar who begs for his freedom from an open cage, never realizing that his own not-knowing is the only bar that keeps him in.

I watched a beggar at the station who sat in the same corner for years though he had been offered work, simply because he didn't believe things could change; it made me think of a cage with its gate open.
mind in darkness
I trusted a fake guru's advice for years because I simply didn't know enough to question him, and it cost me a lot.
doha on how ignorance keeps ppl stuck in wrong beliefs
The unlit mind loves its own illusions as a child loves a tale, and cries when it is taken away.
Write a doha explaining that the darkness of not knowing is not a lack of facts but a mistaking of the false for the true, so a person may be clever and still wander blind, quite sure of his way.

Give me a doha about a chakor bird that cannot tell milk from the white of dawn and sips at nothing, a picture of the unknowing person who takes the false for the true and starves beside real nourishment.
doha with milk n chakor bird: ignorant ppl cant tell real from fake
My nephew drank a fake milk-like drink for months thinking it was healthy, and he reminds me of a chakor bird chasing a mirage; I'd like a doha on such not-knowing.
The chakor bird mistakes white mist for milk and drinks the air; the unknowing too are fed on appearances.
milk, chakor bird, ignorance
He takes the moon for the sun and the sun for a fever; the unknowing mind swaps day and night without a doubt.

I'd like a doha about a person who cannot tell the moon from the sun, awake when he should sleep and sleeping when he should wake, showing how ignorance reverses everything and makes the false seem true.
moon, sun, not knowing
I kept the hours of the moon and slept through the sun for a whole year, sure it was right, and only now see how wrong I had been.
doha: ppl who confuse the sun n the moon, i.e. clueless
Write a doha about a cuckoo that settles in an inn for one night and believes it is its own, not knowing the dawn will send it on, a picture of the unknowing taking the borrowed for the owned.
doha: cuckoo thinks the inn is its own lol
The cuckoo sings in the inn as if its walls were its own, never knowing the morning will take the room.
My cousin sings so happily in a rented place, convinced it will be his forever, like a cuckoo at an inn, and no one dares tell him the lease ends soon.
cuckoo, inn, ignorance
jaggery, forehead mark, ignorance
Craft a doha about someone who thinks a mark on his forehead makes him holy and a lump of jaggery makes his words sweet, but inside he is bitter and blind, taking outward show for real worth.
Jaggery on the lips, a mark upon the brow; the unknowing think the sweet and the sacred are only skin deep.
doha: forehead mark and jaggery, clueless ppl think show = real
My uncle puts a mark on his forehead each morning and speaks sweet as jaggery, and people take him for a saint, though he's blind to his own cruelty; doha?
doha: clueless ppl dont realize everyone ends on a bier
He plans for centuries while the bier waits patiently; such is the sleep of the unknowing.

Please make a doha about a man who builds castles in the air and schemes for generations, ignorant that his own bier is already being prepared, a picture of how not-knowing makes people take the fleeting for the lasting.
bier, not knowing
My neighbour just started a huge new project at eighty-five, planning for decades with total certainty, as if a bier were never in his future; I don't know whether to laugh or weep.
doha: clueless man cuts the tree he sits on
He cuts the very tree that shades him, and calls it clever; such is the daylight of the unknowing.
My cousin sold off the old family tree for quick cash, thinking it only a nuisance, never knowing what it gave us all those years.

Write a doha about a man who sits on a branch of a tree and saws it from under himself, a picture of the person in the darkness of not-knowing who destroys his own support while thinking himself wise.
tree, ignorance
I grew up beside a river, always dreaming of living in a palace, not knowing that the peace I had was worth more; a doha on that kind of blindness?
The one who lives beside the river thirsts for a palace; such is the sleep of the unknowing.
river, palace, ignorance
I need a doha about a man who leaves the river that feeds him to chase a palace he has seen in a dream, ignorant that what he abandons is real and what he seeks is only an illusion.
doha w river n palace, mistaking false for true

Can you put together a doha about a man who circles the temple again and again seeking light outside, not knowing that the darkness is within him, because ignorance makes him take the outer rite for the inner knowing.
He walks around the temple a thousand times, and the dark within him walks along unseen.
doha: ppl go to temple but r still clueless inside
temple, not knowing
My aunt visits the temple every day and yet still can't tell fact from superstition, and I'm sad she's so sure.
I thought I understood how the world works until a crisis showed me I had barely touched the surface; it was like standing on the shore of the ocean and thinking I had seen it all.
ocean, not knowing
Write a doha about a frog in a small pond who has never seen the ocean and swears the pond is all there is, a picture of the unknowing person who takes his tiny world for the whole truth.
doha: ignorance is thinking ur puddle is the ocean
The ocean rolls beyond the horizon, and the one who has never seen it swears his small pond is the world.
My brother talks so confidently about things he knows nothing about, tongue running like a moth drawn to a brightness, and gets burned each time; doha idea?
Give me a doha about the tongue that praises what it has never tasted and the moth that dives at a bright thing, a picture of the person in the dark of not knowing who is fooled by appearances.
The tongue boasts of what it never knew; the moth seeks glitter and is lost; both are children of the dark.
tongue, moth, ignorance
doha w tongue + moth about ppl being fooled by looks
I reached for what looked like a beautiful lotus on a pond and got scratched by a thorn on the stem, and it reminded me how we grab at things without knowing.
lotus, thorn, ignorance
doha: clueless ppl grab the lotus n get the thorn
The unknowing reaches for the lotus and feels the thorn; the surface was never the whole.

I'd like a doha about how not-knowing makes a person admire the lotus and ignore the thorn beneath, taking the beautiful for the harmless and the bright for the real, until he is hurt by what he did not see.
doha: clueless ppl bang on the wrong door
door, not knowing
My neighbor kept knocking at a shut door for an hour, convinced someone was in, and wouldn't hear that the place was empty; it made me think about stubborn not-knowing.
He knocks and knocks at the door of the empty dwelling, and the dark of not-knowing answers him.
Write a doha about a man who pounds on a door that leads nowhere while the real entrance stands open behind him, a picture of the unknowing person who takes the false way for the true.
ignorance, false mistaken true

Craft a doha for students who feel certain about their answers, gently warning them that not-knowing does not feel like not-knowing, but like certainty, and that a false belief held with confidence is the darkest night.
The darkest night is not the one without light, but the one the sleeper calls day.
I always thought I understood my partner perfectly until she left, and then I realized I had never actually known her at all.
doha on not knowing that u dont know
The unknowing one decorates his house and never opens the window to himself.
house, not knowing
My father spent his savings renovating our house but never noticed that the family inside was falling apart; blind to what mattered.
Please make a doha about a man who polishes the walls of his house but never looks into the dark rooms of his own mind, since not-knowing makes him take the outer shine for the inner health.
doha: clueless ppl clean the house but ignore themselves
The cloud promises and passes; the oil press grinds and gives; the unknowing mistake the one for the other and go hungry.
doha w cloud + oil press: mistaking promise for substance
Write a doha about a man who watches a cloud and expects it to give oil, while the oil press that really gives is ignored, a picture of how not-knowing makes people chase the empty promise.
cloud, oil press, ignorance
My brother keeps hoping luck will bring him money like a cloud passing by, while ignoring the oil press of steady work that could really feed him; doha?
washerman, bell, ignorance
doha: clueless ppl think the bell cleans them like a washerman
A washerman near our colony rings a bell at the gate each morning believing it brings luck, though he never questions why; he is so sure.
The washerman rings the bell and thinks the stain will fall away; the unknowing trust the sound and not the scrub.
I need a doha about a washerman who rings a bell over dirty clothes instead of washing them, believing the sound will cleanse, a picture of how not-knowing takes the ritual for the real labor.
The moth chases the shadow of brightness and burns; so the unknowing chase the shade of things and call it life.
I chased an image of success for ten years, like a moth after a shadow, and ended up with nothing.
Can you put together a doha about a moth that circles the shadow of a light on the wall and thinks it has reached the source, a picture of the unknowing person who takes the shadow for the substance.
doha: moth chasing shadows, ignorance
moth, shadow, not knowing
A washerman in our lane stands still as a heron at the water's edge, but his mind is busy with envy, and he thinks nobody sees; doha on such blindness?
doha: heron n washerman, looking pure but clueless inside
The heron stands in white, the washerman scrubs in white; both are pure outside, and neither knows the dark within.

Write a doha about a heron that stands in white and a washerman who scrubs everything white, yet inside they are ignorant of their own stain, showing how the unknowing take outward whiteness for inner purity.
heron, washerman, ignorance
Give me a doha about a bird in a cage who thinks the grindstone's turning is the whole world, unaware the cage limits its view, a picture of the unknowing mistaking a small view for everything.
doha w cage and grindstone, not knowing
Between cage and grindstone, the unknowing turn and grind, and call the little round of days the whole of life.
I have been grinding at the same job for twelve years, in a cage of routine, and I never noticed it was my own belief that kept me there.
cage, grindstone, ignorance
physician, cotton, ignorance

I'd like a doha about a patient who takes cotton for medicine and trusts a quack for a physician, because the darkness of not-knowing makes him take the false for the true and the harmful for the helpful.
He plugs his ears with cotton and calls the quack a physician; the dark of not-knowing hears nothing true.
My uncle ignored a real physician because he preferred a fake who packed his wound with cotton and sweet words, and it still pains me.
doha: clueless ppl trust quacks over a real physician, with cotton
doha about how stubborn not-knowing is
false seen as true
My friend swears by a theory he has never tested, and every time I show him proof he just gets angrier.

Write a doha reminding us that the unknowing cling to their mistaken beliefs more tightly than the wise cling to the real, since darkness does not know it is dark and the false feels very much like the true.
In the hush of the unlit mind the false sits honored, and the true knocks softly in vain.
The pearl gleams in the oyster-dark, and the unknowing pass over it to pick glass.
pearl, ignorance
I tossed out an old pearl necklace from my grandmother, thinking it was a cheap imitation, and later learned it was real; doha on that kind of mistake?

Craft a doha about how a man who has never seen a pearl sees only a pale round thing and throws it away, a picture of how not-knowing fails to recognize the precious and mistakes the false for the true.
doha: pearl or glass? clueless ppl cant tell
fire, not knowing
Fire is at his feet, and still he sleeps; the unknowing call the blaze a warm bed.
doha: clueless guy sleeps while fire spreads
My father ignored every warning about the old wiring because he was sure he knew better, and it nearly cost us everything in a fire.
Please make a doha about a man who plays happily while the fire of the world burns around him, unaware of danger because the darkness of not knowing hides it, and he calls the blaze a festival.
Write a doha about a man whose tongue boasts of a palace he has never seen, praising what he does not know, a picture of the unknowing who speak loudly of what they have never understood.
tongue, palace, ignorance
A boy in our colony brags about palaces and foreign cities he has never visited, and everyone believes him because he talks with such certainty.
doha w tongue n palace, big talk with no knowing
The tongue builds palaces in the air, and the unknowing move in and dwell there.
The unknowing press sand for oil and wait for the lamp to burn; no light comes, yet they blame the dark.
sand, lamp, ignorance
I kept pouring effort into a doomed venture like pressing oil from sand, certain a lamp would light, and never questioned my own assumptions.
doha: clueless ppl try to get oil from sand to light a lamp
I need a doha about a man who tries to squeeze oil from sand to light his lamp, and curses the darkness for not lifting, a picture of the unknowing who take the false for a true source.
I trusted the wrong person for so long that now I wonder how I could have been so blind, and I'd like a doha about that kind of not knowing.
short doha: not knowing makes us believe lies
darkness of not-knowing
Can you put together a doha about a mind unlit by understanding that builds a world of false beliefs and lives in it happily, never suspecting its walls are made of its own mistakes.
A dream believed as fact; the unknowing feast on the idea of a feast.
doha: clueless guy cleans the house w a winnowing fan but doesnt see the mess inside
The winnowing fan sifts the grain; the house is swept; but the dark of the unknowing mind is left untouched.
house, winnowing fan, ignorance
My mother sweeps the house every morning and sorts the grain with a winnowing fan, but she has never questioned a single belief she inherited; I'd like a doha.
Write a doha about a person who winnows grain with a fan and keeps his house spotless, yet never sifts the false beliefs out of his own mind, because the darkness of not-knowing hides them from him.
need a doha on ignorance and false beliefs, simple words pls
I used to ridicule my cousin's doubts, but he was right and I was wrong, and I felt how thick my own not-knowing was.
Where understanding has not dawned, the false walks about as if it were the true.
Give me a doha about how not-knowing is not a lack of cleverness but the failure to see things as they are, and how the unknowing take what appears for what is, and call their confusion clarity.
unknowing, mistaking
My neighbour watches a bee circle a pile of ash in his yard, hoping for honey, and shakes his head at it, yet he does the same with his own life; doha idea?
I'd like a doha about a bee that circles a heap of ash expecting honey, a picture of the person in the dark of not-knowing who seeks sweetness in what is dead and takes the false for the true.
ash, bee, ignorance
The bee hums over ash and calls it blossom; so the unknowing seek sweetness in what has burned.
doha w ash n bee, clueless ppl seek honey in the wrong place
Write a doha about a parrot that repeats holy words it does not understand, a picture of the person who recites without knowing, taking the sound for the meaning, and the false for the true.
My cousin recites verses fluently like a parrot but couldn't tell you one thing they mean, and he's very proud of it.
The parrot repeats the sacred phrase and the dark of not-knowing still sits upon its beak.
doha: parrot reciting stuff without knowing the meaning
parrot, ignorance
